units.explain: Normalizes an optional numeric seconds value to a timedelta. Given None or an already-timedelta value it returns the input unchanged; an int (or other non-timedelta value) is wrapped as timedelta(seconds=value). Pure function, no state or exceptions beyond what timedelta(seconds=...) raises for invalid inputs.
units.summary: Convert int seconds to timedelta; pass through None or timedelta unchanged.
uncertainties: Non-int, non-timedelta values are accepted by the type signature relaxation and delegated to timedelta(); exact failure text unproven here.

units.explain: Class-level configuration surface of App (the sansio base of Flask). It declares overridable classes and defaults: aborter_class (werkzeug Aborter), jinja_environment (flask templating Environment), app_ctx_globals_class (_AppCtxGlobals), config_class (Config), url_rule_class (Rule), url_map_class (Map), test_client_class/test_cli_runner_class (None until set), json_provider_class (DefaultJSONProvider), and an empty mutable jinja_options dict. Three ConfigAttribute descriptors expose config keys as properties: testing→TESTING (bool), secret_key→SECRET_KEY, permanent_session_lifetime→PERMANENT_SESSION_LIFETIME with _make_timedelta as a get_converter. should_ignore_error is a deprecated class attribute set to None (see separate disposition). Changing jinja_options after first access of jinja_env has no effect; changing these class attributes after app construction may or may not affect already-created instances depending on which member reads them.
units.summary: Declares App's pluggable classes, defaults, and config-backed attributes.

extras.note: jinja_options is a shared class-level dict; mutation affects all instances until reassigned.

uncertainties: Whether subclasses overriding these class attributes are re-read lazily by consumer code outside this file is unproven.

units.explain: Constructs the app. It first delegates to Scaffold.__init__ with import_name, static_folder/static_url_path, template_folder, and root_path. It then resolves the instance path: the instance_path argument must be an absolute path (ValueError otherwise) or defaults to auto_find_instance_path(). It builds config via make_config(instance_relative_config), an aborter via make_aborter(), a JSON provider instance from json_provider_class, and initializes empty registries: url_build_error_handlers, teardown_appcontext_funcs, shell_context_processors, blueprints (ordered dict by name), extensions. It creates the URL map as url_map_class(host_matching=host_matching), stores subdomain_matching, and sets _got_first_request=False which later gates setup methods. No returns; ValueError propagates for a relative instance_path.
units.summary: Initializes instance path, config, aborter, JSON provider, and app registries.

extras.note: Relative instance_path raises ValueError before any registries are created.

uncertainties: Exact behavior of Scaffold.__init__ for root_path detection lies outside this file.

units.explain: Guard used by setup-time methods: if the app has already handled its first request (_got_first_request is True) it raises AssertionError naming the method f_name, explaining that late setup changes would be applied inconsistently. Returns silently otherwise.
units.summary: Raises AssertionError when setup methods are called after the first request.

units.explain: Cached property returning the display name of the application. If import_name is '__main__', it reads __file__ from the __main__ module, returning '__main__' when unavailable, otherwise the file's basename without extension. For any other import_name it returns it as-is. The result is cached by werkzeug's cached_property, so later changes to import_name do not affect an instance that already accessed this.
units.summary: Application display name; derived from the run file when import_name is __main__.

units.explain: Cached property returning a standard logging.Logger for the app, created by flask.logging.create_logger(self) and named after the app. Per its documented contract: level is DEBUG in debug mode, and a default handler is added only if none are configured. Because it is cached, the logger is created once per instance.
units.summary: Lazily creates and caches the app's standard Logger.
uncertainties: Handler/level setup details live in flask.logging and are not verifiable from this source.

units.explain: Cached property returning the Jinja environment, creating it on first access by calling create_jinja_environment(). Because create_jinja_environment is abstract here (raises NotImplementedError) and jinja_options is only read at creation time, changes to jinja_options after first access have no effect. Concrete subclasses (flask.app.Flask) supply the real factory.
units.summary: Lazily creates and caches the Jinja environment on first access.

units.explain: Abstract hook in this sansio base: unconditionally raises NotImplementedError. Subclasses must override to build the Environment from jinja_options and create_global_jinja_loader(). Grouped here because it has no independent logic.
units.summary: Abstract; subclasses must supply the Jinja environment factory.

units.explain: Creates the Config instance assigned to self.config. Uses root_path, or instance_path when instance_relative is true, and copies default_config as defaults, overriding DEBUG from the environment via get_debug_flag(). Instantiates self.config_class(root_path, defaults). Only failure propagation is whatever config_class or get_debug_flag raise.
units.summary: Builds the Config object rooted at the instance path or app root.

units.explain: Factory returning an instance of aborter_class (default werkzeug Aborter) with no arguments; the object is invoked by flask.abort and directly. Simple, no branching.
units.summary: Creates the Aborter instance used by flask.abort.

units.explain: Locates the instance folder when none was passed to the constructor. It calls find_package(import_name); if no installation prefix is found it returns <package_path>/instance, otherwise <prefix>/var/<name>-instance where name is the app's name property. Behavior depends on find_package and cached name resolution.
units.summary: Guesses the instance folder next to the package or under var/ for installed packages.

relations.basis: f"{self.name}-instance" reads the name cached property

units.explain: Returns a DispatchingJinjaLoader wrapping this app, which dispatches template loading between the app loader and registered blueprints' loaders. Docstring discourages overriding this; overriding jinja_loader is preferred.
units.summary: Builds the dispatching Jinja loader across app and blueprints.

units.explain: Decides autoescaping per template name. None (unknown name) enables autoescaping; otherwise the filename is lowercased and checked for extensions .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml, .svg (case-insensitive as of 3.2). Pure predicate, no side effects.
units.summary: Enables Jinja autoescape for HTML/XML/SVG templates and unknown names.

units.explain: Property pair mapping the debug flag onto the DEBUG config key. The getter returns config['DEBUG']; the setter writes config['DEBUG'] and, if TEMPLATES_AUTO_RELOAD is still None, sets jinja_env.auto_reload to the new value — meaning the setter touches jinja_options-derived state and triggers jinja_env creation on first set. Docstring warns the flag must be set early and never in production.
units.summary: Debug flag backed by the DEBUG config key, syncing Jinja auto-reload.
uncertainties: Exact timing effects of setting DEBUG late (per docstring 'may not behave as expected') are not implemented in this file.

units.explain: Setupmethod-decorated registration of a Blueprint with optional keyword overrides (url_prefix, subdomain, url_defaults, name, etc.). After recording, it delegates entirely to blueprint.register(self, options); the options are also reachable in Blueprint.record callbacks via BlueprintSetupState. The name option (2.0.1+) allows registering the same blueprint multiple times under unique names.
units.summary: Registers a blueprint, delegating setup to Blueprint.register.

units.explain: Returns self.blueprints.values(), a ValuesView over registered blueprints in registration order. Registration count is not tracked; a blueprint registered under multiple names appears multiple times.
units.summary: Iterates registered blueprints in registration order.

units.explain: Registers a URL rule (setupmethod-guarded). Endpoint defaults to the view function's name via _endpoint_from_view_func when not given. Methods come from the options or the view's methods attribute, defaulting to ('GET',); a plain string raises TypeError. Method names are uppercased into a set, and required_methods from the view plus OPTIONS (when provide_automatic_options applies) are unioned in. provide_automatic_options resolution order: explicit argument, then view attribute, then 'OPTIONS not in methods and config PROVIDE_AUTOMATIC_OPTIONS'. A url_rule_class rule is constructed with the merged methods/options, its provide_automatic_options flag set, and added to url_map. Finally the view function is stored under the endpoint; if an endpoint already maps to a different function, AssertionError is raised stating the mapping would overwrite an existing endpoint function. Mutates url_map and view_functions.
units.summary: Validates and registers a URL rule and its view function on the URL map.

extras.note: Duplicate endpoint with a different view function raises AssertionError.
methods passed as a bare string raises TypeError with usage guidance.

uncertainties: Whether url_map.add validates rule/endpoint conflicts internally is outside this file.

units.explain: Overloaded decorator registering a Jinja filter. If called with a callable directly (no parentheses), it registers immediately under the function's __name__ and returns the function. Otherwise it returns a decorator that registers under the given name (or the function's name when None) and returns the function unchanged. setupmethod-guarded; registration delegates to add_template_filter, which touches jinja_env.
units.summary: Decorator registering a function as a Jinja filter, usable bare or with a name.

units.explain: Setupmethod that inserts the function into self.jinja_env.filters under the provided name or the function's __name__. Accessing jinja_env here freezes jinja_options for that instance.
units.summary: Registers a Jinja filter directly in the environment.

units.explain: Same pattern as template_filter but for Jinja tests: when the first argument is callable, registers it immediately via add_template_test and returns it; otherwise returns a decorator registering under the given name (defaulting to the function's __name__) and returning the function. setupmethod-guarded; added in 0.10.
units.summary: Decorator registering a function as a Jinja test, usable bare or with a name.

units.explain: Setupmethod inserting the function into self.jinja_env.tests under name or f.__name__. Touches jinja_env and therefore finalizes jinja_options.
units.summary: Registers a Jinja test directly in the environment.

units.explain: Same overloaded decorator pattern for Jinja globals: callable argument registers immediately via add_template_global and is returned; otherwise a decorator is returned that registers under the optional name (defaulting to the function's __name__) and returns the function. setupmethod-guarded; added in 0.10.
units.summary: Decorator registering a function as a Jinja global, usable bare or with a name.

units.explain: Setupmethod inserting the function into self.jinja_env.globals under name or f.__name__. Touches jinja_env and therefore finalizes jinja_options.
units.summary: Registers a Jinja global directly in the environment.

units.explain: Setupmethod decorator appending the function to teardown_appcontext_funcs and returning it unchanged. Documented contract: functions run when the app context pops (end of request, CLI command, or with-block exit); on unhandled exceptions they receive the error object unless an errorhandler already handled it; return values are ignored; teardown functions must not raise.
units.summary: Registers a callback run when the app context is popped.

units.explain: Setupmethod decorator appending the function to shell_context_processors and returning it unchanged; processors supply variables when a shell context is created.
units.summary: Registers a function providing shell context variables.

units.explain: Finds the error handler for an exception using a documented priority: blueprint handler for the specific HTTP code, app handler for that code, blueprint handler for the exception class, then app handler for the class; None if nothing matches. It resolves (exc_class, code) via Scaffold._get_exc_class_and_code(type(e)); blueprints is an ordered candidate list of blueprint names. When a code exists, code-specific lookups run before generic (None-code) lookups; for each (code, name) pair it iterates the exception's MRO looking in error_handler_spec[name][c], returning the first non-None handler. Empty maps are skipped. Relies on error_handler_spec structure defined on Scaffold.
units.summary: Locates the best-matching error handler by code, then class, blueprint-first.
uncertainties: Ordering guarantees depend on the caller-supplied blueprints list and error_handler_spec layout in Scaffold; graph resolved the .get call ambiguously, so dict-get behavior is read from source only.

units.explain: Decides whether an HTTP exception raised by a view should bypass its error handler and surface as a normal traceback. Returns True when config TRAP_HTTP_EXCEPTIONS is set. Otherwise: if TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is None (unset), debug mode is on, and the exception is a BadRequestKeyError, it is trapped (debug convenience); if TRAP_BAD_REQUEST_ERRORS is truthy, any BadRequest is trapped; otherwise returns False so handlers run. Called by Flask.handle_user_exception per the graph. The adjacent class fragment assigns should_ignore_error = None, a deprecated no-op hook (3.2) that previously suppressed errors from teardown handlers.
units.summary: Decides if an HTTP exception should skip its error handler and propagate.

extras.note: should_ignore_error is a deprecated attribute fixed at None; no logic reads it in this file.

units.explain: Creates a redirect response by delegating to werkzeug's redirect with the app's response_class, so the returned object matches the app's response type. Since 3.2 the default status code is 303 (was 302). Called by flask.redirect; parameters are location URL and code.
units.summary: Builds a redirect response using the app's response class.

units.explain: Mutates the passed values dict in place by invoking registered url_default_functions before URL building. It always starts with the app-level (None-key) functions; when the endpoint is dotted, it also derives blueprint names from the dotted prefix via _split_blueprint_path (reversed so innermost-blueprint defaults apply appropriately), because this may run outside a request context where request.blueprints is unavailable. Functions are called as func(endpoint, values) and any values they set persist.
units.summary: Applies registered URL default functions to endpoint values before building.

units.explain: Invoked by url_for on BuildError. Iterates url_build_error_handlers calling each with (error, endpoint, values); a handler returning None is skipped, a handler raising BuildError replaces the active error (kept in the error variable for use after the except block), and the first non-None return value is returned to url_for. If all handlers fail or the list is empty, the error is re-raised: bare 'raise' when handling the currently active exception (preserving traceback), otherwise 'raise error' for the passed-in exception. Returns str per signature.
units.summary: Runs URL build error handlers, re-raising BuildError if none resolve it.

relations.basis: error parameter typed BuildError; except BuildError handler

uncertainties: Whether any handler return type other than str is coerced is not handled here; typed as returning str only.
